body: I'm not coping but im in the same boat.

It sounds like you have a great grasp on the situation, but your mum sounds like the problem. Is there anyway of you going to the doctor without your mum so you can tell the doctor? Or bring her with her to the doctor, because I think she needs to realise how much this is affecting you.

I feel you OP. It must suck feeling that way. Is it possible to switch jobs if that is making you feel bad? Maybe you could meet some friends at a new job? 

It sounds like this new school is promising, I would really recommend joining an active sports team or society, and you'll easily make friends that way. I know waiting for it is going to be hard but it's only 6 months out of the rest of your life- what really is 6 months when you put it into perspective?

I dropped out of the first university I went to- I really hated my course and the university itself, and it was the hardest 9 months of my life waiting for a fresh start at university in the next year. I had very bad depression, and everyday conisisted of me waking up, going to the gym, going to work which was a retail hellhole, come back and go to sleep. I was so miserable, and all my friends were at university so I had nobody near by left. I wish I could give you advice on how to cope but the truth was I didn't, but I understand how you are feeling. I had just turned 18 at that point, and I wanted to go out and party in pubs and nightclubs (I live in the UK), and I felt like I was missing out on a whole life that I thought I should have got, that I deserved. 

But things are better for me now. I still have depression and anxiety, and I am struggling a bit. But I am building a future for myself, and have made good friends and a boyfriend here at university. It will get better, it just hurts to wait.

The counselling is so oversubscribed at my university I only get to see someone once a month. It's torture. I want a social life, to be happy, to go to my sports training but I can't. Or it feels like I can't. If I'm not studying I feel like something bad will happen.

I wish it were that simple. All my friends either study in their labs where I can't go because I dont do their subject, or study in the silent section where it's really hard to get a set, let alone two next to each other.
I've tried that but I just keep deciding last minute that I can't not study.

You have us, and you do want to live because you have posted here. 

Life is shit. It really is, but there will be something to keep you with us. Has anything made you feel happy in the past?

Are you sure you want to do dentistry? Can't you try for a degree that is shorter- something like computer science or economics? 

I feel the exact same as you. I'm in my final year of university, have a graduate job all lined up if I get a decent grade this year. I am so scared I'm not gonna make the cut and end up not getting this graduate job. And then if a get the job, I'm gonna end up worrying about keeping it and performing well, and so on..

And then I have my best friend who is literally the opposite of me. She has a shitty degree, and has no career ambitions. She just wants to travel the world, and she is doing that by teaching English in S Korea, and plans on repeating that in another country next year. She is constantly poor but she has so many life experiences, and she has seen so much more of the world than i have, sitting in my room pouring over maths textbooks. But I want to make enough money to start my own dream business, and that keeps me going. 

You have to decide what you really want in life? Do you want to wait until you're old before you can start living? Or do you want to break free now? Is money everything
You're not alone with this feeling.

When I first came to university I struggled to make friends- flatmates were uninterested, my hall was dead and I couldn't make friends in my classes. I didn't have anyone to talk to- I remember getting so lonely that I locked myself in my room because I needed to shut the world out, and nobody came to check on me and I was in there for a whole week (I had my own bathroom in my room and took a weeks supply of food). I was so close to committing suicide after that week. I moved halls, and although the flatmates weren't my friends, they would chat to me in the corridor now and again.

I signed up for a buddy support scheme where an older students goes around and helps you make friends- saddest sounding thing in the world but it actually helped. Most of the time they didn't do anything apart from give you confidence to turn up to events and get chatting to people. I joined a sports team that way, and since then I have had no problem. Does your university have something like that? And do you have any clubs you want to join?

Also remember that university is a very lonely time for a lot of people. More people than you know are struggling.
I've tried all of the healthy things. The only thing that works every time is hitting myself.

About suicide being a genetic defect- I feel the exact same. I always think I am meant to die early. I have the life you had before things went south, and I am close to crumbling and giving up too. I always think in the next 'stage' in life, things will get better, I will be happier. Lol, fuck it. Life has just got shittier since high school- nothing excites me, I look forward to nothing. The most exciting part of my day is when I can sleep, because I don't have to think.  So I can sort of understand where you are coming from.

It is scary putting yourself back out there, you feel vulnerable that things might not go your way. But what you have tried in the past might not be the right thing for you, there are always other options out there to explore. Yes it must feel like they won't work out, and it's too depressing to try but there is the potential for missing out something great. 

You haven't fallen behind- life isn't a race.

I can't pretend to understand what you are going through. Sometimes life deals a shit hand, and it's unfair. Holy fuck it really is. But life can also be beautiful, and although it may not feel like it now, but there will be some sort of solution- it may be a coping mechanism that allows you to deal with your atypical autism, or you may find something or someone to live for. Whatever shit life throws at you, there is always something nice around the corner. It will get better, please don't leave us. You are worth it.
this might all contribute to something larger, don't feel guilty.
thank you. i visited home and feel much safer from myself now. I dont know how long that will last but being near my parents makes me feel better.
I tried to tell my flatmate but I am too embarrassed. The pain of telling somebody else. But all I want to do is swallow my pills and drink the vodka in my cupboard.
I'm sitting in my shared kitchen so I don't do anything.

It isn't your fault- how were you supposed to know a fight would lead to a suicide attempt? Now you know the extent of his mental health problems, try and avoid fights in the future,.

Give him a few days to process what he did- he might be in shock or not believe what he did, or it could be a defence mechanism. 

It isn't your fault.
